doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: John Pendleton, Claymore Williams and David Jones in California
summary: They talk of John Pendleton, Claymore Williams and his brother the baritone player, and trying to find David Jones in California.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: You know John Pendleton, didn't you?
No, I heard talk about him.
Well, you know John Pendleton. Yes. John Pendleton. He used to play trombone. Trumpe. He used to play trumpe?
Yes. There's a whole lot of like... I speak like two-row. Two-row was a... You know old man Claymore Williams? You getting any information on him at all?
Yes, we've heard people up at Donaldsonville.
Yeah, and his brother... Tell me his brother was one of the greatest biotone players. It was George. George, that's right.
He played trombone too, didn't he?

I think he was a biotone. But he was... No honest... But I... Did he play trombone too? I didn't know. He played trombone. I think somebody told me... But I know he was one of the... They said he was one of the greatest biotone players. He was. Zilp had a miss. And you didn't meet... You all didn't get in touch with David Jones in California. No, we missed him.
And you couldn't find Wade Willie, you say? No.
I'm afraid Wade is dead maybe, but Jones is still out there. I know, Ed.
He was there when I was there. He was doing... He was a maintainer's man in some place. He moved...
He moved a couple of times, and I couldn't get his address until about the last day I was there. And then he didn't have a phone.
No, can't go further back, Papa. He was the wall itching.
